title: Week 28 Check-In · The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
description: This week you read Chapters 10 to 12: Father Christmas comes to Narnia, the snow melts into spring, and Peter fights his first battle. You practiced apostrophes in contractions and words that show belonging, the word parts com- and con- (they mean with or together), and endings that change a base word. Show what you know!

questions.text: Which sentence uses the apostrophe the right way?
options: It’s spring in Narnia at last.
Its’ spring in Narnia at last.
Its spring in Narnia at last.
questions.from: 28.1 Think it through (it’s and its), 28.4 DOL

questions.text: Write each contraction as two words: can’t, didn’t, wasn’t.
questions.from: 28.1 Now check your thinking (can’t = can + not), 28.1–28.3 passages
questions.status: fixed (they’ve swapped for wasn’t; the week only teaches n’t contractions)

questions.text: Write two sentences about what happens in Narnia in Chapters 10 to 12. Use one contraction and one word that shows belonging, like Peter’s.
questions.status: kept (now asks for both apostrophe jobs)

questions.text: The word parts com- and con- both mean with or together. Break apart the word combine. What does it mean?
questions.from: 28.1 See what was hiding, 28.2 match, 28.3 build
questions.status: new (old Q4 tested the root script, not taught this week)

questions.text: Which word means “to join two things together”?
Choose one: company, connect or conversation. Write a sentence that shows what the word means.
questions.status: new (old Q6 used script, describe, inscription)

questions.text: Which word is spelled the right way?
questions.status: new (old Q7 asked students to underline a root)

questions.text: Some endings change the base word before they go on: double the last letter, drop the silent e, or change y to i. Explain one of these changes, and give an example.
questions.from: 28.1 Now name the pattern, 28.4 Which Change Dice
questions.status: new (old Q8 asked about the root script)

questions.text: One word is spelled wrong. Which one?
What is happening to Narnia in this passage? Use two details from the passage.
questions.status: kept (passage is now the book’s own words)

questions.text: Why is the dwarf so worried when he says “This is Spring”? What does spring mean in Narnia?
questions.status: fixed (old Q11 said the Witch spoke this line; it was the dwarf)

questions.text: The melting snow is a symbol of hope coming back. What other symbol of hope can you find in Chapters 10 to 12? Explain what it stands for.

Model sentence from the book: “And then, as he looked at one tree he saw a great load of snow slide off it and for the first time since he had entered Narnia he saw the dark green of a fir tree.” A small detail (the green of one tree) stands for something big (winter is ending). Write your own sentence where a small detail stands for something bigger.

Choose one image from Chapters 10 to 12 (the melting snow, Father Christmas’s gifts, or the spring flowers). Write 1–2 sentences about what it stands for in the story. Use a word like represents, suggests or symbolizes.
questions.status: kept (green buds swapped for spring flowers, which are in the book; literary verbs from 28.2)

passage.title: Reading passage (The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, Chapter 11)
passage.text:
The trees began to come fully alive. The larches and birches were covered with green, the laburnums with gold. Soon the beech trees had put forth their delicate, transparent leaves. … A bee buzzed across their path.
“This is no thaw,” said the dwarf, suddenly stopping. “This is Spring. What are we to do? Your winter has been destroyed, I tell you! This is Aslan’s doing.”
— C.S. Lewis, The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, Chapter 11
